channel.title: koray.dev — writing
channel.description: Koray Güler — founder and product engineer. Fintech, applied AI, and small teams. Notes on money, models and shipping alone.

item.title: Evals before prompts
item.description: For a year I wrote prompts the way I once wrote code without tests: carefully, confidently, and with no way of knowing when I broke something. Writing the eval first fixed that, and it cost less than an afternoon.
item.author: id@koray.dev (Koray Güler)

item.title: Ledgers are append-only opinions
item.description: Why every fintech eventually writes its own ledger, and how to make peace with that. A balance is not a number you store; it is an argument you can replay.
item.author: id@koray.dev (Koray Güler)

item.title: The token budget of a checkout flow
item.description: What an LLM actually costs when it sits on the critical path of a payment — measured in milliseconds and in incidents, not in cents per million tokens.
item.author: id@koray.dev (Koray Güler)

item.title: Shipping alone: my build loop
item.description: The exact week-shape that lets one person run three products without lying to themselves about what got done.
item.author: id@koray.dev (Koray Güler)

item.title: Turkish IBANs and the joy of boring code
item.description: A 200-line library, 40 test cases, and zero incidents in two years. A short argument for writing the unglamorous thing yourself.
item.author: id@koray.dev (Koray Güler)

item.title: We chose Postgres over a queue
item.description: Sometimes the boring database is the whole architecture. What we replaced, what it cost, and the numbers two years later.
item.author: id@koray.dev (Koray Güler)
